channel.title: Nature Communications
channel.description:
Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, health, physical, chemical and Earth sciences. Papers published by the journal aim to represent important advances of significance to specialists within each field.

We are committed to providing an efficient service for both authors and readers. Our team of independent editors make rapid and fair publication decisions. Prompt dissemination of accepted papers to a wide readership and beyond is achieved through a programme of continuous online publication.

item.title: [7] Layer-number-parity-dependent abnormal magnetic ordering in few-layer CrI3 on N-face AlN substrate
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Wei Ji, Lun Dai

Authors: Jiamin Chen, Jiahao Chen, Cong Wang, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Study of magnetic ordering and electronic doping in 2D van der Waals materials.

Tags: #2Dmaterials #magnetism #vanderWaals

Abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 08 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74019-7 The authors demonstrate that N-face AlN substrate induces layer-number-parity-dependent magnetic multistates in CrI3. 5L-CrI3/AlN evolves through distinct magnetic multistates (+ 5 → –1 → +1 → –5); first-principles calculations attribute this effect to interfacial hole doping.

item.title: [7] Metal-insulator transition at low densities in a two-dimensional low-bandgap semiconductor
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Oleg V. Yazyev, Ahmet Avsar

Authors: Ali Al Mejamai, Thiti Taychatanapat, Johan Félisaz, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Fundamental study of metal-insulator transition in a low-dimensional electronic system.

Tags: #metal-insulatortransition #2Dmaterials #semiconductors

Abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 08 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74097-7 The behavior of metal-insulator transitions can be impacted by interaction and disorder mechanisms. Here, the authors identify metal-insulator transitions at carrier densities on the order of 1010 cm−2 in PtSe2 devices and evidence of a crossover in the metal-insulator transition behavior.
